# Document service architecture

This example service is a teaching model, not a source-verified map of this repository.
Follow the same Client, Document API, and Document Store from the overview to the details.
The request latency is $T = T_{api} + T_{store}$.

$$
T_{store} = T_{queue} + T_{write}
$$

The client sends a complete document, not a patch.

```typescript
const request = { title: "System guide", blocks: [] };
await client.replaceDocument(request);
```

slides.explanationMarkdown:
The Client submits a document to the Document API.
The Document Store owns persistence.
This overview omits validation and storage steps; the next slides add them without renaming these components.

slides.title: Document API detail
slides.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  Client["Client"] --> Api["Document API — 文件 API"]
  subgraph ApiDetail["Document API internals"]
    Api --> Validator["Request Validator — check the complete document before any storage operation"]
    Validator --> Handler["Request Handler"]
  end
  Handler --> Store["Document Store — 工作區文件儲存與版本資料"]
slides.explanationMarkdown:
The Document API now contains a Request Validator and a Request Handler.
The long validator label and the Chinese API and storage labels are rendering fixtures.
The Document Store remains one node here; the next slide expands its write path.
The example assumes validation runs before persistence.
